title: Shadow failback timing exposed circuit-breaker coordination gap causing SLO misses
creator: Lukas Meyer
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 we observed a multi-region SLO regression affecting API latency p99 for hosted text-generation. A staggered failback from the DR region to primary region coincided with a shadow (non-primary) region reintroduction: overlapping routing changes plus asynchronous circuit-breaker state caused a brief amplification of requests to a small subset of hot shards. That amplification pushed token processing beyond our graceful-degradation thresholds and triggered aggressive load-shedding, producing SLO misses and client errors for ~18 minutes. This document captures timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and follow-up action items.
impact: User-facing latency p99 rose from 240ms baseline to 1.8s for affected customers in NA-east and EU-west for ~18 minutes. ~2.3% of requests returned 503/504 or truncated responses during window. Business impact: a handful of enterprise customers reported degraded UX and one observed an automated retry loop increasing downstream costs. SLO category: latency p99 and availability; customer_impact: high.
timeline: 2026-03-01T01:12:00Z - Primary region reported elevated GPU scheduling lag on a subset of shards (autoscaler triggered node replacement).
2026-03-01T01:14:30Z - Traffic was shifted to DR region (eu-central as temporary routing target) per circuit routing policy; no capacity shortage in DR.
2026-03-01T01:20:45Z - Primary region healthy signals returned; control plane initiated failback and started reintroducing primary endpoints.

2026-03-01T01:21:10Z - Shadow routing service began re-registering warm standby endpoints from ap-southeast; control-plane reorder resulted in routing table entries that allowed sticky affinity to prefer a tiny hot shard set.

2026-03-01T01:22:05Z - Circuit-breaker agents in edge proxies had stale state and did not immediately reflect the reduced error-rate on reintroduced nodes; simultaneous short-term duplication of routes routed increased traffic to the hot shards.

2026-03-01T01:23:30Z - Token processing queues on 6 GPU pods crossed soft-shed thresholds; automated load-shedding policy escalated to hard-shed for the affected shard groups. Errors and latency spiked.
2026-03-01T01:32:00Z - Runbook invoked: traffic throttled at global ingress, manual override of affinity rules applied, and three overloaded pods were gracefully drained.
2026-03-01T01:40:00Z - Traffic normalized and p99 latency returned to baseline after circuits re-synchronized and KV-cache priming completed. Post-incident monitoring window verified stable behavior.
root_cause: Coordinated failure between (1) staggered control-plane failback ordering that allowed sticky affinity to concentrate requests on a small set of hot shards, and (2) asynchronous circuit-breaker state propagation across edge proxies and control-plane components. The combination amplified a transient traffic imbalance which then tripped load-shedding heuristics prematurely.
contributing_factors: Control-plane failback sequence did not include a guard to evenly rebalance sticky-affinity mappings during reintroduction.
Circuit-breaker state is propagated via eventual-consistency channels without a fast-path re-sync when topology changes occur.
KV cache warmup for reintroduced nodes was incomplete, increasing per-request compute during early tokens and stressing GPU pods.
Autoscaler replacement activity in primary region coincided with failback which reduced available headroom for transient surges.
mitigation: Immediate: temporarily raised soft-shed thresholds in affected shard groups to avoid hard-shed escalation while draining overloaded pods (Mitigated at 01:32).
Immediate: applied manual routing override to disable sticky-affinity for 5 minutes while control-plane rebalanced endpoints.
Short-term: forced circuit-breaker re-sync across all edge proxies to clear stale fail-open states.
Short-term: enabled prioritised KV-cache priming on newly reintroduced nodes to reduce cold-start token cost.
action_items: Asha Patel: Implement atomic failback orchestration that includes an 'affinity-rebalance' step to prevent concentration on hot shards (due 2026-03-24).
Sophie Chen: Add a fast-path circuit-breaker resync API invoked by control-plane on topology changes; include test harness for race conditions (due 2026-03-17).

DevOps Team (owner: Marco Alvarez): Adjust autoscaler cooldown logic to avoid simultaneous node replacement during failback windows; add simulation for failback+scale events in chaos tests (due 2026-04-07).
Runtime Team (owner: Priya Rao): Implement proactive KV-cache priming hook executed before routing reintroduction; measure priming latency and reduce cold forward token cost (due 2026-03-31).

SRE (owner: Keon Park): Create an incident playbook 'shadow-failback' describing detection signals, immediate mitigations and runbook steps; add automated alert that detects sticky-affinity imbalance (due 2026-03-15).
Product (owner: Maya Thompson): Communicate incident summary to affected enterprise customers and offer remediation support and credits where applicable (due 2026-03-12).
review_notes: Reviewed in postmortem meeting 2026-03-05; engineering leadership accepted root cause and prioritized actions into resilience-2026-q1 roadmap.
